mechanism_narrative: The sharp same-week drops in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and GROCERY_PHARM indicate immediate avoidance behavior that reduces discretionary trips to malls, restaurants, and entertainment venues. If this avoidance persists, RETAIL_REC will remain below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay at or below the current t-0w levels for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT below the recent low marks a regime shift toward restricted movement and canceled outings. That threshold should cut retail visits within one week and keep RETAIL_REC depressed for the following month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15% week-over-week relative to baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week of TRANSIT crossing below -15%, or rebounds despite TRANSIT remaining below that threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recover while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, more commuters leave home but continue avoiding long discretionary stops, so nearby convenience-oriented retail softens rather than rebounds. The interaction predicts a short-lived retail decline over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though WORKPLACES stay above their t-1w level and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained pullback in GROCERY_PHARM signals household stockpiling and fewer auxiliary shopping trips. Those same households then reduce discretionary retail-and-recreation visits, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below the last-four-week average after GROCERY_PHARM stays below -10% for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The earlier positive PARKS values imply weather and leisure conditions that can support discretionary outing demand; if park mobility stays less negative than transit mobility, some outing activity shifts toward retail destinations within one month. This should lift RETAIL_REC only when outdoor leisure remains comparatively resilient.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above TRANSIT for at least two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over 28 days even though PARKS remains above TRANSIT for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If workplaces mobility drops below the current sharp contraction threshold, firms are effectively operating remotely and weekday shopping opportunities vanish. That policy-like labor shock should translate into a further one- to two-week decline in retail-and-recreation mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decrease within 14 days after WORKPLACES moves below -15%, or it rebounds despite continued workplace suppression.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates fewer commuters and fewer midweek chaining trips, which should mechanically reduce incidental retail visits. Because both series already deteriorated in the latest week, RETAIL_REC should stay below baseline over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week average while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below zero for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound from the deep t-0w trough in RETAIL_REC would require households to stop substituting away from public venues and begin normalizing foot traffic. If RESIDENTIAL remains high while PARKS and TRANSIT stay depressed, that rebound will fail and retail mobility will keep falling.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% while PARKS and TRANSIT stay below -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves within one week despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 5% and both PARKS and TRANSIT staying below -10%.
